text: NetHorizon last-mile CVRPTW serves 50 customers from a single depot with six vehicles. Each vehicle has capacity 200 kilograms. Customer time windows sit between 08:00 and 18:00. The planner must minimize total distance plus a lateness penalty of 4.5 per minute.
Minimize sum_k sum_i sum_j c_ij x_ijk + 4.5 sum_i max(0, a_i - l_i). Subject to each customer visited once, vehicle load <= 200, and a_i in [e_i, l_i] with e_i>=08:00 and l_i<=18:00.

from pyomo.environ import *
model = ConcreteModel('NetHorizon_CVRPTW')
model.N = RangeSet(0, 50)
model.K = RangeSet(1, 6)
model.x = Var(model.N, model.N, model.K, domain=Binary)
model.capacity = Param(initialize=200)
# objective: distance + 4.5 * lateness
Solver: OR-Tools routing CP-SAT hybrid. Status: feasible. Best objective 1842.6 km equivalent. Runtime 38.4 seconds. Six routes, max load 196 kg, two customers with 7 minutes slack.

The binding constraints are vehicle capacity 200 kg and the 18:00 close of the city hub. OR-Tools is preferred over a pure MIP because the 50-customer time-window graph is too large for a compact MTZ formulation. If demand grows above 80 customers, switch to ALNS with the same capacity and penalty.
Line-B FJSSP has 20 jobs and 5 machines. Each operation may run on two eligible machines. The production target is a makespan bound of 312 minutes. Dispatching with SPT exceeds 340 minutes.
Minimize Cmax. For each operation o, sum_m y_om = 1 for eligible machines. No-overlap on each machine. Precedence start(o2) >= start(o1)+p_o1m. Cmax >= start+p for all last operations.
# Line-B is solved with CP-SAT, not Pyomo MIP, because disjunctive machine constraints explode. Use ortools.sat.python.cp_model.CpModel with interval variables and AddNoOverlap.
Solver: Google CP-SAT. Status: optimal. Makespan 308 minutes, 4 minutes under the 312 bound. Runtime 12.1 seconds. Machine 3 is the bottleneck with 96 percent utilization.

CP-SAT finds a 308-minute calendar because it reasons over intervals rather than big-M disjunctions. Machine 3 is binding. Adding a sixth eligible machine for coating operations is the first capacity lever.
DC-14 plans 12 SKUs over 8 weeks. Holding cost is 1.20 per unit-week. Setup cost is 450 per changeover. Week-3 demand spike is 1800 units of SKU-NH442. HiGHS is the default open solver.
Minimize sum_t (1.20 I_t + 450 y_t + produce_cost x_t). Inventory balance I_t = I_{t-1}+x_t-d_t. x_t <= M y_t. I_t, x_t >= 0, y_t binary.

from pyomo.environ import *
model = ConcreteModel('DC14_LotSizing')
model.T = RangeSet(1, 8)
model.P = Set(initialize=['SKU-NH442'])
model.hold = Param(initialize=1.20)
model.setup = Param(initialize=450)
model.y = Var(model.P, model.T, domain=Binary)
Solver: HiGHS. Status: optimal. Objective 18640.0. Four setups, inventory peak 420 units after week 3. Runtime 0.84 seconds.
Four setups beat weekly changeovers because the 450 setup dwarfs 1.20 holding. SKU-NH442 should be built in week 2 and week 3 only. If setup falls below 180, weekly production becomes optimal.
Select a subset of 12 plant projects under a shared capex budget of 2.4 million. Project Gamma cannot be chosen with Project Delta (mutual exclusion). Maximize NPV.
Maximize sum_i npv_i z_i. sum_i cost_i z_i <= 2.4e6. z_gamma + z_delta <= 1. z binary.

model = ConcreteModel('CapexKnapsack')
model.I = RangeSet(1, 12)
model.z = Var(model.I, domain=Binary)
model.budget = Param(initialize=2400000)
model.conflict = Constraint(expr=model.z[3] + model.z[4] <= 1)
Solver: CBC MIP. Status: optimal. NPV 3.18 million. Seven projects selected. Gamma chosen, Delta rejected. Runtime 0.05 seconds.
The 2.4 million budget is binding. The Gamma/Delta exclusion is active: Gamma has higher NPV per dollar. A 100k budget increase would add Project Iota, not Delta.
Locate 8 distribution centers among 40 candidate sites to serve 120 stores. Service radius target is 45 kilometers. Unmet demand is forbidden.
Minimize sum_i sum_j d_ij x_ij. sum_j y_j = 8. sum_j x_ij = 1 for all stores i. x_ij <= y_j.

model = ConcreteModel('PMedian8')
model.p = Param(initialize=8)
model.y = Var(model.Sites, domain=Binary)
model.open_limit = Constraint(expr=sum(model.y[s] for s in model.Sites)==8)
Solver: SCIP. Status: optimal. Mean distance 28.6 km. All stores within 45 km. Runtime 6.7 seconds.
p=8 is the smallest count that keeps every store inside 45 km. Closing any of the coastal DCs violates the radius.
GridWest unit commitment covers 24 hours with 6 thermal generators. Spinning reserve must stay at 12 percent of hourly load. Minimum up time is 3 hours. Generator G4 is a slow-start steam unit.
Minimize sum_g sum_t (startup_g v_gt + noload_g u_gt + fuel_g p_gt). Load balance, reserve >= 0.12 load_t, min up 3 hours, ramp limits.

model = ConcreteModel('GridWest_UC')
model.G = RangeSet(1, 6)
model.T = RangeSet(1, 24)
model.u = Var(model.G, model.T, domain=Binary)
model.reserve_frac = Param(initialize=0.12)
Solver: Gurobi-compatible MIP. Status: optimal. Cost 412750. G4 stays on from hour 6 to 22. Runtime 3.9 seconds.
The 12 percent reserve and G4 min-up time force G4 online before the evening peak. A fast-start aeroderivative in slot G7 would cut cost more than relaxing reserve to 10 percent.
Cut 86 rectangular parts from 2800x2070 mm MDF sheets with 3.2 mm kerf. Rotation by 90 degrees is allowed. The nesting target is at most 17 sheets.
Assign each part to a sheet and coordinates (x,y) with no overlap inflated by 3.2 mm kerf. Minimize number of sheets, upper bound 17.
# Geometry packing is a poor MIP. Use CP-SAT 2D no-overlap or a dedicated nester. Kerf 3.2 mm is added to part width and height before placement.
Solver: CP-SAT geometry. Status: feasible. 16 sheets used, 91.4 percent average utilization. Runtime 22 seconds.
Kerf 3.2 mm is the hidden waste driver. Sixteen sheets beat the 17-sheet target. Grain-sensitive parts that cannot rotate need a second pass.
Roster 42 technicians across three shifts for 14 days. Maximum consecutive nights is 3. Each shift needs 9 on-site technicians plus 2 on-call.
Assign binary x_employee,day,shift. Cover >= 9+2. Consecutive night shifts <= 3. Rest after nights >= 24 hours.

model = ConcreteModel('Roster14')
model.E = RangeSet(1, 42)
model.D = RangeSet(1, 14)
model.S = Set(initialize=['day','swing','night'])
model.cover = Param(initialize=11)
Solver: CP-SAT. Status: feasible. All cover constraints met. Night-load Gini 0.08. Runtime 2.2 seconds.
The 3-night cap, not headcount, is binding. Hiring two extra technicians would barely help; relaxing nights to 4 would.
